title: Smoothness at a point of a flat scheme family under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:U\to T$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $h:T^{\prime}\to T$ be any morphism of schemes, and let $a:U^{\prime}=U\times_TT^{\prime}\to U$ and $f^{\prime}:U^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$ be the projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every point $u^{\prime}\in U^{\prime}$, $f^{\prime}$ is smooth at $u^{\prime}$ if and only if $f$ is smooth at $a(u^{\prime})$. Smooth at a point means that the restriction to some open neighbourhood is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. No flatness assumption is imposed on $h$.

source.place: Tag 02V4 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-smooth), case (1), equivalently the pointwise equality of the two smooth loci; proof uses Tag 01V9 and smoothness over field extensions.

proof.text: Fix $u^{\prime}$ and put $u=a(u^{\prime})$, $t^{\prime}=f^{\prime}(u^{\prime})$ and $t=h(t^{\prime})=f(u)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $f^{\prime}$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Flatness of both maps gives flatness of their local ring maps at these points by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus the pointwise fibre criterion will apply to both maps; no flatness of $h$ is needed.

First suppose $f$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $V$ of $u$. The pullback $V^{\prime}=V\times_TT^{\prime}$ is an open neighbourhood of $u^{\prime}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. Its projection to $T^{\prime}$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Check formal smoothness directly from [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: for an affine first-order thickening $Z\subset Z_1$ over $T^{\prime}$ and a $T^{\prime}$-map $Z\to V^{\prime}$, compose to $V$. Formal smoothness of $V\to T$ gives a $T$-map $Z_1\to V$ lifting it. Pair this lift with the given map $Z_1\to T^{\prime}$; their maps to $T$ agree, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a map $Z_1\to V^{\prime}$. Uniqueness in the fibre-product property shows that its restriction is the original map on $Z$. Hence $V^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$ is formally smooth, and therefore smooth by the same definition. This proves ascent.

source.place: Tag 02V4, the inclusion of the inverse image of the smooth locus; Tag 01VB, lemma-base-change-smooth; infinitesimal formulation in Tag 02H0

proof.text: For reflection suppose $f^{\prime}$ is smooth at $u^{\prime}$. Let $v^{\prime}$ and $v$ be the points of $U^{\prime}_{t^{\prime}}$ and $U_t$ corresponding to $u^{\prime}$ and $u$, respectively, using the homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. By [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] and step 1, $U^{\prime}_{t^{\prime}}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t^{\prime})$ is smooth at $v^{\prime}$. Put $k=\kappa(t)$ and $K=\kappa(t^{\prime})$. The residue-field map gives a field extension $K/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] this fibre is $U_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$, and its map to $U_t$ sends $v^{\prime}$ to $v$, since the stated compatibility with the source projections identifies its image with $u$.

source.place: Tag 02V4, proof, first paragraph and displayed fibre-product identity; Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, (1) iff (2)

proof.text: The fibre map $U_t\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Choose an affine neighbourhood $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $v$ with $A$ finitely presented over $k$, using [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. In particular $A$ is a finite type $k$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] its base change $B_K$ is an open neighbourhood of $v^{\prime}$ in the fibre of step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], interchanging the two factors of the tensor product, $B_K=\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k A)$; its projection to $B$ is induced by $j:A\to K\otimes_k A$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Thus if $\mathfrak q_K$ represents $v^{\prime}$, the prime representing $v$ is $\mathfrak q=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$. Restricting the smooth neighbourhood from step 3 to this open proves smoothness at $\mathfrak q_K$ as a scheme point. Restrictions of smooth maps to opens are smooth: in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] local finite presentation restricts, and a lift across a nilpotent thickening still lands in the open because the thickening has the same point set.

source.place: Tag 02V4, affine interpretation of the fibre identity before applying Algebra Tag 02UQ

proof.text: Translate the last smoothness assertion into ring smoothness at $\mathfrak q_K$. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-fibre-affine-ring-at-prime] to $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k A)\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, taking both schemes themselves as affine charts. The fibre at the unique base point is canonically the original scheme, with the structural maps identified, by [lem-weil-pbc-field-base-point-fibre-isomorphism]. The affine fibre ring in that lemma is consequently $(K\otimes_k A)\otimes_K K\cong K\otimes_k A$; multiplication and $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ give the inverse maps. Its kernel prime is exactly $\mathfrak q_K$. Hence $K\to K\otimes_k A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-field-extension-descent] with the finite type algebra $A$ of step 4 and this prime. It gives that $k\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 02V4, proof by Algebra Tag 02UQ (algebra-lemma-smooth-field-change-local), descent implication; affine translation as in Tag 01V9

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-smooth-prime-scheme-neighbourhood] to the fibre morphism $U_t\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with source chart $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$, target chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the smooth prime $\mathfrak q$ from step 5. It supplies a principal open neighbourhood of $v$ on which this fibre morphism is smooth. Thus the fibre is smooth at $v$. Finally [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion], now for $f$ at $u$, gives smoothness of $f$ at $u$: its local finite presentation is a hypothesis, and its local flatness was checked in step 1. This proves reflection, and with step 2 the equivalence. If $U^{\prime}$ is empty there is no point to check.

source.place: Tag 02V4, proof, second paragraph: case (1) by Tag 01V9
